hens_rule_text: Up to 3 fowl without a permit. With an annual Animal Maintenance Permit ($25) you can keep 4 to 12 fowl (up to 25 pigeons). These limits apply to residential lots under 5 acres.
permit_notes: No permit for 3 or fewer fowl. An Animal Maintenance Permit ($25, renewed yearly) is needed for 4 to 12 fowl. No more than three kinds of animals may be kept at one address.
setback_notes: Enclosures for small animals must be 10 feet from the property line if they are within 50 feet of a neighboring dwelling. Coops must also meet the Wichita-Sedgwick County Unified Zoning Code.
coop_rules: Coops and pens must meet zoning rules and be kept in good repair; waste from animal shelters must be disposed of at least weekly.
zoning_notes: Limits cover residential premises under 5 acres. Larger residential properties should contact Animal Control (316-350-3360). Roosters, guinea cocks and peacocks are prohibited.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.

sources.name: City of Wichita, Animal Maintenance Permit information (08/24)

research_notes: Facts come from the city's official Animal Maintenance Permit handout (dated 08/24), which cites Code 6.04.157 to 6.04.159; the Municode text itself could not be opened from this location. Slaughter is not addressed.
